and a curve that is tangent to the \(x\)-axis at \(x=3\), as shown in the figure above. On the interval \(0<x<6\), the
function \(f\) is twice differentiable, with \(f^{\prime \prime}(x)>0\).
(a) Is \(f\) differentiable at \(x=0\) ? Use the definition of the derivative with one-sided limits to justify your
answer.
(b) For how many values of \(a,-4 \leq a<6\), is the average rate of change of \(f\) on the interval \([a, 6]\) equal to 0 ?
Give a reason for your answer.
(c) Is there a value of \(a,-4 \leq a<6\), for which the Mean Value Theorem, applied to the interval \([a, 6]\),
guarantees a value \(c, a<c<6\), at which \(f^{\prime}(c)=\frac{1}{3}\) ? Justify your answer.
